observations: Sony mirrorless camera body in a red silicone protective skin.
The camera body has 'SONY' and 'alpha 7 III' markings visible in photo 0.
A black zoom lens is shown detached from the camera in photo 0 and photo 1.

The camera's articulated screen is shown in an open position in photo 1, but it is powered off.
All photos contain a watermark: 'POSTED ON JIJI BABARAY TV'.

No photos show the camera powered on, the sensor, or the rear screen displaying an image.
The lens is visible, but the focal length and aperture markings on the barrel are not legible in the photos.
photo 2 shows the box and accessories for a Godox V1-S flash.

risks.risk: Sensor damage, scratches, or excessive contamination.
risks.proof: A clear, high-resolution photo of the camera sensor with the lens and cap removed.
risks.if_unproven: as a damaged sensor requiring replacement

risks.risk: High shutter count indicating heavy professional wear.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count from an online tool using a recent RAW file.
risks.if_unproven: as a high-mileage unit near mechanical failure

risks.risk: Lens optical defects such as fungus, haze, or scratches.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the front and rear glass elements of the lens.

risks.risk: Electronic failure or dead pixels on the screen/EVF.
risks.proof: A photo or video of the camera powered on with the rear screen and EVF active.

proof_requests: Photo of the camera powered on showing the LCD screen and a live image.
Screenshot of the current shutter count.
Clear photos of the lens glass (front and back) and the lens barrel markings.
Photo of the camera sensor without the lens attached.
Confirmation that the Godox flash unit itself is included and functional.
response.reason: The camera body and flash model are clearly identified from the photos. The kit can be priced at its worst-case functional state (non-working) until proof of condition is provided.
